Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Case Quality Evaluation Work (Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2008] No. 6

To: All Higher People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions on Case Quality Evaluation Work (Trial Implementation) of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued to you. Please implement them in light of actual trial work.

January 11, 2008

Supreme People's Court

Guiding Opinions on Case Quality Evaluation Work (Trial Implementation)

For the purpose of objectively and fairly evaluating the trial work of the people's courts, strengthening the trial management of the people's courts, intensifying supervision, and improving trial quality, and in accordance with the Second Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts, the following opinions are hereby proposed for the trial implementation of case quality evaluation work in the people's courts.

I. Unify Thinking, Update Concepts, and Deeply Understand the Significance of Case Quality Evaluation Work of the People's Courts

1. Establishing a scientific and unified case quality evaluation system for the people's courts is an important component of the Second Five-Year Reform Outline of the People's Courts. "Case quality evaluation" means designing a number of evaluation indicators reflecting various aspects of trial justice, efficiency, and effectiveness, using various judicial statistical data and multi-indicator comprehensive evaluation techniques to build a quantitative model for case quality evaluation, calculate a comprehensive index of case quality, and conduct overall evaluation and analysis of the case quality of people's courts at all levels nationwide. This work is of great significance for correctly grasping the trial situation, summarizing trial experience, enhancing trial capacity, improving trial work, and advancing the process of national rule of law construction.

2. Establishing a case quality evaluation system for the people's courts is conducive to: the people's courts' conscious acceptance of supervision from the People's Congress and society, achieving an objective, scientific, and fair evaluation of the people's courts' trial work; strengthening guidance and supervision by higher-level courts over lower-level courts; facilitating scientific decision-making and correct implementation of various reform measures of the people's courts; and improving the quality of trial personnel, enhancing their sense of responsibility in trial work, and promoting a virtuous cycle of trial work.

3. Through the evaluation system, quantitative standards for trial quality of the people's courts can be established, a new dynamic internal supervision mechanism and scientific trial management within the courts can be created, and various factors affecting trial quality can be analyzed, thereby providing complete and detailed reference bases for trial decision-making and management of people's courts at all levels, and promoting the overall improvement of trial quality in the courts.

4. Through the correlation among evaluation indicators, constraints, and the coordination and integration of comprehensive indices, the scientific management of the trial work of the people's courts can be further strengthened, and the justice and efficiency of trials can be maximized.

II. Respect Science, Follow Laws, and Strive to Build a Fair and Reasonable Case Quality Evaluation System

5. Case quality evaluation shall adhere to correct guidance, save litigation costs, and avoid one-sided pursuit of high indicators, interference with judicial independence, or impairment of the litigation rights and other lawful rights and interests of the parties. It shall adhere to the idea of democratic management, and the processes of data collection, aggregation, and organization shall be made open to ensure that the evaluation has good objectivity, predictability, and credibility.

6. To meet the requirements of diversified evaluation purposes, a modular indicator design method shall be adopted. In addition to comprehensive evaluation of trial quality, through the transformation and combination of evaluation indicators and evaluation indices, evaluation of each link of litigation and enforcement, evaluation of various types of trials, and evaluation of the quality of judges' case handling shall be achieved.

7. The evaluation indicator system is divided, according to the needs of trial work management, into three second-level indicators: trial justice, trial efficiency, and trial effectiveness. The second-level indicators consist of 33 third-level indicators.

People's courts at all levels may add or reduce indicators according to actual circumstances.

8. There are 11 indicators for trial justice, composed of: rate of change of case filing; rate of jury participation in first instance; rate of reversal on appeal in first instance; rate of remand for retrial on appeal in first instance; rate of reversal of effective judgments; rate of remand for retrial of effective judgments; rate of open court sessions in second instance; rate of suspension or termination of enforcement; rate of illegal trials; rate of illegal enforcement; and quality indicator of judgment documents.

9. There are 11 indicators for trial efficiency, composed of: rate of case filing within statutory time limit; average number of cases concluded per court employee per year; average number of cases concluded per judge per year; rate of case conclusion; balance of case conclusion; rate of application of summary procedure in first instance; rate of pronouncement of judgment in court; ratio of average trial time to trial time limit; ratio of average enforcement time to enforcement time limit; ratio of average duration of cases not yet concluded to trial time limit; and ratio of average duration of cases not yet enforced to enforcement time limit.

10. There are 11 indicators for trial effectiveness, composed of: rate of appeal; rate of petition; rate of mediation; rate of withdrawal; rate of complaints and petitions; rate of repeated petitions; actual enforcement rate; rate of enforcement subject matter realized; rate of voluntary compliance with judgments; rate of satisfaction with first-instance judgments; and indicator of public satisfaction.

11. In the evaluation, quantitative research methods may be used, and specialized computer programs may be employed to compile a comprehensive index, second-level indices, and third-level indices for case quality evaluation, as well as type indices for litigation and enforcement links and for criminal, civil, and administrative trials.

12. The Supreme People's Court shall, based on the evaluation purpose, the characteristics of trial work, and with reference to the average, maximum, and minimum values of evaluation indicators of courts nationwide in recent years, determine the reasonable value and warning value of evaluation indicators.

13. The weight is a numerical value reflecting the importance of a certain indicator in the comprehensive evaluation system. The Supreme People's Court shall reasonably determine the weights of evaluation indicators based on the evaluation purpose, the importance of the indicators, the potential negative impact, and the reliability of data sources.

People's courts at all levels may appropriately adjust the weights of evaluation indicators according to the work priorities of their respective courts.

14. The Supreme People's Court shall revise the comprehensive index of case quality by applying an adjustment coefficient to address the issue that unbalanced socioeconomic development in different regions may affect the objectivity of the evaluation.

III. Improve Institutions, Rationalize Relationships, and Strive to Enhance the Level of Case Quality Evaluation

15. The case quality evaluation work of the Supreme People's Court shall be the responsibility of the Research Office. Local people's courts at all levels may establish a corresponding management body or designate an existing body to be responsible for it. The evaluation management body shall be responsible for the design of evaluation indicators, data collection and organization, compilation of evaluation indices, and the dissemination and analysis of evaluation results.

Relevant departments and personnel of people's courts at all levels shall actively cooperate and support the evaluation work.

16. Higher-level people's courts shall be responsible for organizing and guiding the evaluation work of lower-level courts, and may conduct evaluations of the case quality of their own courts and courts within their jurisdiction.

People's courts at all levels shall be responsible for the collection, organization, and analysis of evaluation data of their own courts, and shall regularly report basic evaluation information upward.

17. The roles of trial process management, individual case review, legal document review, and judicial statistics shall be fully utilized to achieve reasonable division of labor, complementary responsibilities, data sharing, and ensure the objectivity and authenticity of the evaluation.

18. Data for evaluation indicators shall be collected from the following sources and channels:

(1) Evaluation data shall be based on information generated in trial and enforcement work, as well as their supervision and management activities, including trial process management, legal documents, statistical ledgers, judicial statistical reports, and disciplinary inspection statistical reports.

(2) For evaluating public satisfaction, people's courts at all levels may, as needed, organize or entrust private survey institutions to collect data through questionnaire surveys of deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, integrity (image) supervisors, parties and their representatives (defense lawyers), and the general public.

(3) Socioeconomic data involved in evaluation indicators shall be based on the previous year's government Statistical Yearbook.

19. People's courts at all levels shall establish a standardized database of legal documents and a unified statistical ledger as the basis for verifying the authenticity of evaluation data. The legal documents and statistical ledgers recording the trial process and results shall be automatically extracted and generated by computers from the trial process management information. For courts that have not implemented networked trial process management, legal documents shall be entered into the case information database, and the extraction of case information and generation of statistical data shall be completed synchronously with the trial and enforcement process of the case, and shall be guaranteed to be fully consistent with the records in the case files.

IV. Innovate Mechanisms, Improve Systems, and Fully Leverage the Role of the Evaluation Mechanism

20. Establish and improve a judicial statistical system that is compatible with the development of trial work and the needs of trial management, and unify the names, statistical calibers, statistical timing, calculation methods, and measurement units of judicial statistical indicators.

21. Accelerate data accumulation, and establish a computer database with the case quality evaluation indicator system as the core, reflecting the basic situation of trial work, team building, judicial guarantees, etc., and covering social, political, economic, and cultural aspects, to provide data support for evaluation.

22. Evaluation shall be managed by information technology. The data collection, organization, transmission, and index compilation of evaluation indicators shall be automatically completed and updated in real time by computers to avoid or reduce interference from human factors.

The evaluation computer management software shall be uniformly developed by the Supreme People's Court.

23. People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court, regularly report all types of legal documents and statistical statements recording the trial process and results level by level upward. The reported information shall be complete, truthful, comprehensive, and accurate. Courts with network transmission conditions shall upload information via the network; courts without network transmission conditions shall submit information by burning discs.

24. The Supreme People's Court shall analyze the evaluation data and evaluation indices every half year and annually, forming a national court case quality evaluation analysis report; shall summarize the case quality situation of higher people's courts, intermediate people's courts, and grassroots people's courts, and regularly provide feedback to people's courts at all levels on the case quality evaluation situation.

25. Strengthen verification of evaluation data. Verify the authenticity of evaluation data through the inherent legal requirements and the correlation between judicial statistical indicators. If the verified evaluation data is inconsistent with the reported data, the reporting unit shall state the reasons, and after review and approval by the higher-level court, the data shall be corrected, and the reported data shall be revised according to the error rate.

26. Establish and implement a verification system for evaluation data and a reporting system for illegal statistical acts. The Supreme People's Court shall organize a special inspection of judicial statistical data once a year, randomly select several evaluation indicators, and verify the authenticity of their data.

The verification of judicial statistical data and the investigation and handling of illegal statistical acts shall be reported nationwide within the court system after the inspection is completed.

Any unit or individual that engages in fraud, false reporting, concealment, or tampering with statistical data for the purpose of pursuing evaluation indices, if the circumstances are serious and the impact is adverse, shall be subject to Party discipline and administrative sanctions by the disciplinary inspection and supervision departments in accordance with relevant provisions.

27. Evaluation is a brand-new task in court management. Evaluation results are a comprehensive reflection of the trial work of the people's courts and are one of the important bases for trial work management, decision-making, and the evaluation and assessment of people's courts at all levels. Courts at all levels shall correctly treat the evaluation results, attach great importance to the comprehensive utilization of evaluation data, regularly analyze the situations and problems reflected by the evaluation, identify weak links in work, strengthen supervision and guidance, and continuously improve trial work.

In the evaluation work, attention shall be paid to collecting opinions and summarizing experience, with particular emphasis on conducting research on the use of evaluation indicators, weights, evaluation methods, and comprehensive indices, and putting forward opinions and suggestions suitable for court management and conducive to scientific evaluation, which shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court to promote the continuous development of evaluation work.
